                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the effect that mutations in different parts of the respiratory tract have on susceptibility to infection. A mutation in the gene encoding for the CD21 protein is induced in a sample of cells obtained from the nasopharyngeal epithelium. This mutation is most likely to prevent infection with which of the following viruses?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Rhinovirus
opb. Epstein-Barr virus
opc. Human immunodeficiency virus
opd. Cytomegalovirus
ope. Parvovirus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
A mutation in the CD21 gene leads to impaired B cell activation, decreased complement receptor type 2 (CR2) expression, and impaired B cell co-stimulation, resulting in reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus. Evidence paths confirm the interaction between CR2 and B-Lymphocytes, supporting the reduced susceptibility to Epstein-Barr virus.
